agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-03a verification: item (vi), the retry.backoff_seconds sub-finding of the inert-accepted-fields half
summary_for_principal:
This closes one of five sub-parts of another checklist item (declared settings the system accepts but doesn't act on). A background research pass this session re-verified all five by reading the actual code, not by trusting an earlier report — two turned out riskier or more open-ended than first thought and are being handled separately; this is the one that was a clean, mechanical fix.

When a step's automated tool call fails in a way that's expected to be temporary, the system retries it. The document format lets a process author declare how long to wait before retrying, doubling each time — but that setting was silently ignored: every retry fired back-to-back with no pause at all, no matter what was declared.

Fixed: retries now actually wait, doubling each time, exactly as documented. Proven with a test that confirms the exact wait times.

Full test suite: 366 passed, 1 new (a pre-existing retry test also updated so it doesn't now take a real 2-second pause every run).

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. Four sub-parts of this checklist item remain, plus three unrelated items — continuing next unless you'd rather reprioritize.

also.reason: New regression test asserting exact backoff timings via a patched asyncio.sleep; confirmed the patch target didn't even exist before the fix. A pre-existing retry test updated to stub asyncio.sleep too, so it stays fast.

interpretation.ask_as_given: Verify item (vi)'s 'inert accepted fields' half: fields the schema/model accept but the engine doesn't act on at runtime. A background research pass identified retry.backoff_seconds as one of five such fields, confirmed genuinely inert by direct code reading (grep across src/ finds it only in the schema, model, and unused default constant).
interpretation.read_as: Of the five findings, fix the ones that are mechanical and low-risk now; defer the ones needing a real design decision (an open spec question, or a change with the same replay-correctness hazard class this session already hit four times) to their own separate passes rather than rushing all five into one PR.

filled_in.gap: The spec says backoff_seconds is 'the starting delay before exponential backoff' but does not state the exact multiplier or whether there's a maximum delay cap.
filled_in.assumed: Delay before the Nth retry = backoff_seconds * 2^(N-1) — the plainest reading of 'starting delay' (the first retry waits exactly backoff_seconds) 'before exponential backoff' (doubling from there). No cap applied, since the spec states none and inventing one would be guessing a rule the format doesn't ask for.
filled_in.grounded_in: CLAUDE.md: 'survive the bad-but-conformant attack' cuts both ways here — inventing an uncited cap would itself be an uncited rule; the literal spec wording supports this formula without needing one.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — a one-line formula; changing the multiplier or adding a cap later touches only this one computation.

filled_in.gap: Whether to sleep inline inside the same next()/report() call, or return a 'retry after N seconds' signal for a later call to resume, isn't stated by the spec's own four-call contract (§12.1).
filled_in.assumed: Sleep inline — the engine is already fully async end to end, so this only delays the one coroutine handling this call, not the event loop or any other concurrent run; a caller-facing contract change (a new answer kind or field) is a materially bigger surface change than this pass's own narrow scope.
filled_in.grounded_in: CLAUDE.md's 'adopt the cheap seam now; defer the expensive guess' and 'keep PRs to one reviewable concern' — the inline sleep is the narrowest change that makes the spec's stated behaviour true, without redesigning the call contract on a guess about what future callers might need.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — two-way door; removing the sleep call returns to immediate redispatch, and a future 'retry later' contract change could still be layered on top without touching this formula.

decisions.headline: D31 — a TRANSIENT retry now waits retry.backoff_seconds (or the format default), doubling on each successive retry, before redispatching; before this fix backoff_seconds was accepted, parsed, and otherwise completely unused.
decisions.problem: RetrySpec.backoff_seconds was accepted by the schema, parsed into the model, and carried by every StepNode/Tool, but nothing in engine/run.py ever read it — both retry re-dispatch sites (_advance_step's fall-through, _record_step_result's recursive call) redispatched immediately with no delay, regardless of what backoff_seconds said or defaulted to.
options_rejected: Return a 'retry after N seconds' signal to the caller and let a new next()/report() call redispatch later: rejected for this pass — widens NextAnswer's own shape for every existing caller to handle, a bigger surface change than this pass's narrow scope, and nothing in §12.1's four calls anticipates a 'come back later for this same in-flight attempt' response today.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — a local variable, a one-line formula, and one await asyncio.sleep(...) call; no schema or durable-record shape change.

evidence.claim: Before the fix, engine/run.py had no `import asyncio` at all and no reference to backoff_seconds anywhere outside the schema/model/defaults — confirmed by grep across src/ and by the new test's monkeypatch target not existing pre-fix.
evidence.source: grep -rn backoff_seconds src/; tests/engine/test_run.py::test_transient_retry_waits_with_exponential_backoff, run against the unfixed engine, this session (failed with ModuleNotFoundError for the monkeypatch target, the strongest possible confirmation no mechanism existed).

evidence.claim: After the fix, two consecutive TRANSIENT failures then a success, with backoff_seconds=1.0, produce recorded sleep calls of exactly [1.0, 2.0] before the second and third dispatch attempts.
evidence.source: Same test, passing after the fix.

evidence.claim: retry.max (the sibling field governing how many retries are allowed) was already correctly enforced at both sites before this fix and is unaffected by it.
evidence.source: src/sulis_workflows/engine/run.py, lines computing max_retries at both retry sites — read and confirmed unchanged by this diff.

lessons.maxim: When one checklist item bundles several 'inert field' sub-findings, verify and triage all of them together before writing any code — some may be mechanical fixes, others may hide open spec questions or design-level hazards, and knowing which is which up front prevents starting an implementation that turns out to need a design decision halfway through.
lessons.incident: A single background research pass covering five candidate inert fields found: one mechanical fix (this PR), one that can't be refused because the spec's own worked example already uses it and needs real design work (invalidates), one with a genuine spec ambiguity (note_into's decider-kind scope), one needing a new public API surface (ClaimsPort.renew), and one needing a spec clarification before implementation (loop.counts). Triaging all five up front, before writing any code, made it possible to ship the one clean case immediately rather than getting partway into a harder one first.
lessons.destination: This run record's own triage; the remaining four sub-findings are each parked with their own specific blocker named, ready for their own dedicated passes.
lessons.proposed_check: Before starting code on a batch of related findings, sort them by whether they need a design decision or spec clarification versus being a straightforward wiring fix, and do the straightforward ones first as their own separate PRs.
